internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all three occurrences جيب names the chest-level opening of a worn garment — the front slit through which the head/neck passes, into which Moses inserts his hand (27:12, 28:32) and over which women draw their head-coverings (24:31). It is the garment's aperture, not the body it exposes and not the cloth that covers it. The singular/plural difference is purely referential (one man's garment vs many women's garments), not a shift in meaning.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: NOT the body part (chest/breast/bosom-flesh): a hand is put فِى it and cloth is drawn عَلَىٰ it, both presupposing a clothing feature distinct from the flesh — the body's private parts are separately named فُرُوج/عَوْرَات in the same verse 24:31. NOT the covering garment (خُمُر is the cloth drawn over the jayb, not the jayb). NOT an inherent 'concealment/hiddenness' component (in 24:31 the jayb is a site of potential exposure that must be covered; concealment comes from خُمُر/ضرب, not from jyb). NOT a verbal/eventive or abstract/moral sense (root surfaces only as a concrete noun). NOT a generic opening/pocket at large — always the neck/breast opening of a worn garment.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 24:31:18:1 (جُيُوبِهِنَّ) is the sole token outside the near-verbatim Moses doublet: it is plural, in a legal (not miracle) register, and it carries the entire cross-class bridge from 'aperture a hand is inserted into' (فِى, 27:12/28:32) to 'opening a covering is drawn over' (عَلَىٰ). It also admits a rival referent — nothing Quran-internal forces juyūb to mean the cloth-aperture rather than the bodily bosom it exposes — so the whole unity claim rests on this one under-attested, mildly ambiguous verse. It does not contradict the nucleus (same physical locus, both frames satisfied by one garment opening), so it is an adversarial boundary and breadth limit, not a resistant sub-class.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: 'jayb = the bosom/chest region of the body' (body-locus rather than garment-aperture): it fits all three (hand to bosom; cover bosoms). Rejected as primary because it is vaguer than the evidence licenses — فِى + a verb of insertion (أَدْخِلْ/ٱسْلُكْ) with a hand as object demonstrates an aperture one reaches into, not a solid body-region, and in 24:31 a covering (خُمُر) is drawn عَلَىٰ an opening precisely because the jayb is a gap. Per the narrowness principle the garment-aperture reading dominates; but with only 3 tokens the body-locus reading cannot be fully excluded, which is the main reason the grade is capped below STRONG.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three tokens are nominal (form N), single root, splitting only by grammatical number into singular جَيْب (27:12, 28:32) and plural جُيُوب (24:31). The two singular tokens are a near-verbatim narrative doublet (only أَدْخِلْ↔ٱسْلُكْ differs), so the corpus supplies effectively two independent contexts, not three. Both prepositional frames (فِى insertion, عَلَىٰ covering) reduce to one physical object — a chest-level garment opening — viewed from two functional angles; the differing prepositions track differing actions, not differing referents, so the classes are bridged and there is no unbridged split. The account is adversarially clean (no resistant sub-class; sharp in-verse contrast against فُرُوج/عَوْرَات/خُمُر in 24:31) which lifts it above WEAK, but it is not broad (single form-class, n=3, ~2 contexts, one carrying the bridge alone) and one body-locus competitor survives on the thin data — per contract STRONG requires broad distinctive adversarially-clean evidence, so MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE is the honest ceiling. No occurrence is universally established, so scope is REPRESENTATIVE over a single concrete nominal lexeme (LEXICALIZED_CLASS), not a ROOT_GENERALIZATION.

layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: No resistant occurrence and no unbridged class. The only residual is breadth/under-attestation: the cross-class bridge and a surviving body-locus competitor both hinge on the single ambiguous token 24:31:18:1, which caps the result at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE rather than leaving anything genuinely unresolved.

hard_cases.reason: Only token outside the Moses doublet, only plural token, and sole carrier of the cross-class bridge; its عَلَىٰ frame is neutral between garment-aperture and bodily bosom, so it is the single wedge against a unified nucleus — a breadth/under-attestation limit, not a contradiction.

evidence_basis.statement: 24:31:18:1 (جُيُوبِهِنَّ) is the sole token outside the near-verbatim Moses doublet and carries the entire cross-class bridge from 'aperture a hand is inserted into' to 'opening a covering is drawn over'; its عَلَىٰ + خُمُر frame is neutral between the garment cloth-aperture and the bodily bosom it exposes, so the unity claim rests on one under-attested, mildly ambiguous verse without being contradicted by it.

hard_case_representation.rationale: There is no resistant sub-class and no occurrence contradicts the nucleus, but 24:31:18:1 is a genuine adversarial boundary: it alone bears the sg→pl bridge and admits a body-locus rival referent. This is recorded as an EVIDENCE_DERIVED hard case (ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY) whose statement also appears as the strongest_counterexample and in the 24:31 cluster/override notes; it justifies the breadth cap to MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE rather than an UNRESOLVED result.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal occurrence of ج ي ب in which the referent cannot be the neck/breast opening of a worn garment — e.g. a token requiring the bodily chest/bosom itself, a generic non-chest opening or pocket, a covering-cloth sense, or a verbal/abstract sense — thereby breaking the single garment-aperture nucleus or splitting the singular and plural into unbridged classes.
rejection_condition.search_location: All three attested tokens (27:12:4:1, 28:32:4:1, 24:31:18:1) and any newly confirmed jyb occurrence; specifically the governing preposition and verb (فِى + insertion vs عَلَىٰ + covering) and the in-verse contrast set فُرُوج/عَوْرَات/خُمُر in 24:31.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Re-read the governing syntax of each token: confirm whether the object is entered into (aperture), draped over (opening at a surface), or predicated as body/flesh; test whether the body-locus competitor is forced rather than merely admissible, and whether the sg/pl referents remain the same physical garment feature.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Discount the 27:12/28:32 near-verbatim doublet as one context, not two; separate the garment feature (jayb) from the body it exposes (فُرُوج/عَوْرَات) and from the covering cloth (خُمُر); do not import classical-lexicon 'pocket' or body-part 'bosom' glosses as authority; treat عَلَىٰ as neutral evidence that cannot by itself decide aperture-vs-bosom.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If such a token is found, downgrade from a single bridged nucleus: either narrow to an OCCURRENCE_LEVEL claim per surviving class or, if two senses have no Quran-internal bridge, move research_state to UNRESOLVED with claim_scope_kind UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY; if the body-locus reading is forced anywhere, replace the garment-aperture nucleus with the broader body-region account.

reopen_conditions: If any future-confirmed jyb token governs a verb of insertion (أدخل/سلك-type) with a non-garment or non-chest target, or predicates jayb as the body/flesh itself, re-test whether the aperture nucleus still holds or must yield to the body-locus competitor.

If a jyb token appears with عَلَىٰ + a covering in a context where the covered thing is unambiguously the bodily bosom (not a garment opening), re-examine whether 24:31's juyūb should be re-read as body-region, collapsing the garment-aperture reading.

If a jyb token appears outside the clothing domain (a generic opening, receptacle, or verbal/abstract use), reconsider whether the singular جَيْب and plural جُيُوب remain one bridged lexeme or must split into unbridged classes.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The garment-aperture nucleus was tested against (a) the preposition asymmetry فِى vs عَلَىٰ, (b) the body-locus competitor, and (c) the sg/pl split. All three tokens are positively accounted for with no failing occurrence: فِى + verb of insertion forces an aperture over a body-region, عَلَىٰ is consistent with drawing a covering over that same opening, and the sg/pl difference is purely referential. Distinctiveness holds via the in-verse contrast against فُرُوج/عَوْرَات (body parts) and خُمُر (covering). The surviving body-locus reading is a breadth/narrowness residual on n=3, not a refuting occurrence, so the account returns SUPPORTED.
